description: The ad promised money, handled well: corrects the ad, finds the current plan still fits, customer keeps it.

notes.reason_for_inquiry: Saw a TV ad about a $150/month grocery allowance.
notes.findings: Only Summit Rewards HMO has a $150/month allowance; it needs diabetes, CHF or COPD plus care management. He has none of these.
notes.options_discussed: Keep Riverbend Essentials HMO; Maple Value HMO ($50/quarter OTC, specialist $35).
notes.rationale: Current plan keeps Dr. Okafor and covers his drugs at a $0 premium; the ad benefit doesn't apply to him.
notes.next_steps: Keeping his current plan. No change.

lines.speaker: learner
lines.text: Thanks for calling Larkspur Benefits Group, this is Sam. This call is recorded.

lines.speaker: customer
lines.text: I saw a TV ad that said everybody with Medicare can get $150 a month for groceries. I want that.

lines.speaker: learner
lines.text: I can look into that with you. Before we go further: we do not offer every plan available in your area. Currently we represent 3 organizations which offer 6 products in your area. Please contact Medicare.gov or 1-800-MEDICARE to get information on all of your options.

lines.speaker: learner
lines.text: Are you looking to talk about Medicare Advantage plans today, or other kinds of coverage too?

lines.speaker: customer
lines.text: Medicare Advantage. The grocery thing.

lines.speaker: learner
lines.text: First, what plan do you have now, and do you have any other insurance, like from a former employer or the VA?

lines.speaker: customer
lines.text: I'm on Riverbend Essentials HMO. Honestly, it's been fine. No other insurance.

lines.speaker: learner
lines.text: Which doctors do you see, and is there anyone you'd want to keep? Which office do you go to?

lines.speaker: customer
lines.text: Dr. Samuel Okafor at Cedar Street Family Medicine in Millbrook. Twelve years. I'm not changing doctors.

lines.speaker: learner
lines.text: And your prescriptions, with the strength and how often you take each?

lines.speaker: customer
lines.text: Lisinopril 20 milligrams, rosuvastatin 10 milligrams, amlodipine 5 milligrams. Three months at a time.

lines.speaker: learner
lines.text: Once a day each? And which pharmacy fills them?

lines.speaker: customer
lines.text: Once a day. Cedar Street Pharmacy, next door to Dr. Okafor.

lines.speaker: learner
lines.text: Any conditions you're treated for, like diabetes, heart failure or COPD?

lines.speaker: customer
lines.text: Just blood pressure and cholesterol.

lines.speaker: learner
lines.text: Here's the straight story on that ad. The only plan near you with a $150 monthly allowance is Summit Rewards HMO, and it's only for members with diabetes, chronic heart failure or COPD who join a care-management program. With blood pressure and cholesterol, you wouldn't get it.

lines.speaker: customer
lines.text: So the ad was baloney.

lines.speaker: learner
lines.text: It's real for some people, just not for everybody the way the ad made it sound. Your Riverbend Essentials HMO still has Dr. Okafor in network for 2027, and lisinopril, rosuvastatin and amlodipine are all covered. It has a $0 premium, and you keep paying your Part B premium either way.

lines.speaker: learner
lines.text: Maple Value HMO also has a $0 premium and adds a $50 a quarter over-the-counter allowance. Dr. Okafor is in that network too. You'd give up a plan you know works, and your specialist copay would go from $30 to $35.

lines.speaker: customer
lines.text: Eh. I'd rather keep what I've got.

lines.speaker: learner
lines.text: That's completely your decision, and keeping your plan fits what you told me. If you change your mind, the Annual Election Period runs through December 7, and any change would start January 1, 2027.

lines.speaker: customer
lines.text: Good. Thanks for being straight with me.
